deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It appears to be a wrapper, cover slip, or reused scrap, written sideways. It carries the following inscriptions.

(1) Ink, at the top: "Fries. Wahrscheinlichkeitsrechnung. Braunschweig 1842", underlined. This is a bibliographic reference to Jakob Friedrich Fries, 'Versuch einer Kritik der Principien der Wahrscheinlichkeitsrechnung' (Braunschweig: Vieweg, 1842). It reads like a book title noted for borrowing or reading, perhaps as a library request slip.

(2) Pencil: a short line, poorly legible, that seems to begin "Aufs[atz?] ..." and contains the numbers "3." and "5)". It is bracketed by a curved stroke. It may be a reference to a section, volume or page, but I cannot read it reliably.

(3) A large pencil flourish, shaped like a long diagonal stroke ending in a loop (resembling an 8 or g). It is probably a paraph or doodle, not a symbol with mathematical meaning.

(4) Red pencil: "M. 22. 57." This is plausibly an archival or shelf mark. Less likely, it is a date, which could be read as 22 March 1857 ("Mrz"/"M.") or as a numbering "M 22 57". I cannot resolve which.

(5) Ink, at the right: "B. Riemann" followed by an address line beginning "b. G[ä]rbermstr. ...". This means 'at the house of master tanner ...'; the surname is hard to read. It looks like a lodging address of the kind written on a library loan slip or on an addressed cover.

(6) A small numeral, read by the machine transcription as "26"; it may be the archival folio/page count, possibly "36".

The surrounding pages bear no mathematical relation to this sheet. The previous page has algebra on products of ξ, η, ζ and the pairings of 1..8 (combinatorics of theta characteristics / bitangents type). The next page has constant counts with p = (m-1)(n-1) - r. So nothing on this sheet needs reconstructing or checking. Its only content of interest is biographical: it records Riemann's interest in Fries's critique of the foundations of probability, and his lodging with a tradesman.

results.what: Bibliographic note referring to J. F. Fries, Versuch einer Kritik der Principien der Wahrscheinlichkeitsrechnung (Braunschweig 1842), apparently as a book to borrow or read, together with Riemann's name and lodging address.

deep.surprise_reason: There is no mathematical content. The only point of interest is a small biographical detail: evidence that Riemann noted or borrowed Fries's probability book. This fits his known philosophical interests (Herbart, epistemology) but is minor.
transcription_corrections: The signature line reads 'B. Riemann' (machine: 'B.[?] Riemann'). The address line begins 'b. G[ä/e]rbermstr.', meaning 'bei Gerbermeister'. The surname after it is not clearly 'Schultz'; it is uncertain and should be marked [?].
The red pencil mark is 'M. 22. 57.'; it is possibly a date (22 March 1857) or an archival mark.
The small numeral in the middle may be '36' rather than '26', judging by the folio numbering of adjacent pages (35, 36); it is uncertain.
The pencil line beneath the title is largely illegible. Only 'Aufs...', '3.' and '5)' are fairly secure; the rest should be marked [illegible].
The 'large pencil flourish' is a single long diagonal stroke ending in a loop, resembling a large 8 or g, not text.
